posts.title: Bernard MacLaverty to receive Bob Hughes Lifetime Achievement Award
posts.description: Bernard MacLaverty to receive Bob Hughes Lifetime Achievement Award The An Post Irish Book Awards have announced that acclaimed Belfast-born writer, Bernard MacLaverty, is the recipient of the 2026 Bob Hughes Lifetime Achievement Award . The award will be presented to him at the annual An Post Irish Book Awards Gala Awards Dinner in Dublin on 1 st December. As the 2026 Lifetime Achievement honouree, Bernard MacLaverty will join a host of distinguished recipients including former President of Ireland Michael D. Higgins, Anne Enright, Sebastian Barry, Colm Tóibín, Thomas Kinsella, Eavan Boland, John Montague, JP Donleavy, Paul Durcan, John Banville, Maeve Binchy, John McGahern, Edna O’Brien, William Trevor, Seamus Heaney and Jennifer Johnston . Over a literary career spanning almost five decades, MacLaverty, who now lives in Glasgow, has established himself as one of Ireland’s most respected contemporary writers. posts.title: Children’s Booker Prize announce shortlist
posts.description: Eight books shortlisted for the £50,000 inaugural Children’s Booker Prize include two Irish authors and one Irish publisher The eight shortlisted titles for the inaugural Children’s Booker Prize have been announced. They include War by Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin , illustrated by Giovanni Rigano , and Hometown by Shaun Tan . Séamus Almost Famous written by Jessica Scott-Whyte , illustrated by Becka Moor and published by Gill Books is the only Irish-published book on the list. The 2027 prize celebrates the best contemporary fiction for children aged eight to 12 years old, written in or translated into English and published in the UK and/or Ireland between 1 November 2025 and 31 October 2026. The judging panel chose the shortlist from 89 submissions. posts.title: Drumcondra & its changing relationship with the city
posts.description: Drumcondra and its changing relationship with the expanding city is explored by Ruth McManus in a new publication from the Royal Irish Academy Drumcondra , by Ruth McManus , is the third volume in the Irish Historic Towns Atlas Dublin suburbs series. Published by the Royal Irish Academy in association with Dublin City Council , it explores the development of one of Dublin’s best-known suburbs and its changing relationship over time with the expanding city. Following previous atlases of Clontarf and Rathmines , Drumcondra follows the established methodology of the Irish Historic Towns Atlas, combining detailed historical research with maps, photographs, illustrations and a comprehensive topographical gazetteer. At the heart of the publication is a particularly rich cartographic and topographical record. Historic maps appear alongside specially prepared thematic maps, early photographs and illustrations, supplemented by detailed information on more than a thousand suburban sites. Streets
